pp:ec:2011:q2.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ec:2011:q2.question:
A transmission line of characteristic impedance 50 W is terminated by a 50 $\Omega$ load. When excited by a sinusoidal voltage source at 10 GHz, the phase
difference between two points spaced 2 mm apart on the line is found to $\frac{\pi }{4}$ radians. The phase velocity of the wave along the line is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text { Phase difference }&=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \text { (path difference) } \\ \Rightarrow \frac{\pi}{4}&=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\left(2 \times 10^{-3}\right) \\ \therefore \quad &=8 \times 2 \times 10^{-3} \\ &=16 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m} \\ f&= 10 \mathrm{GHz}=10 \times 10^{9} \mathrm{Hz} \end{aligned}$$

Hence the phase velocity of wave along the line is,

$$\begin{aligned} & v=f \lambda=10 \times 10^{9} \times 16 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \therefore \quad v &=1.6 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q3.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ec:2011:q3.question:
An analog signal is band-limited to 4 kHz, sampled at the Nyquist rate and
the samples are quantized into 4 levels. The quantized levels are assumed to be
independent and equally probable. If we transmit two quantized samples per
second, the information rate is ________ bits / second.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Quantized levels are equiprobable; hence

$$\begin{aligned} H&=\log _{2} 4=2 \text { bits/sample }\\ r&=2 \text{samples/sec} \\ \end{aligned}$$

Hence information rate $R=r \cdot H=2 \text{ samples/sec}$

$\times 2\text{ bits/sample}$

$\Rightarrow R=4 \mathrm{bits} / \mathrm{sec}$

pp:ec:2011:q11.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 11
pp:ec:2011:q11.question: The circuit shown below is driven by a sinusoidal input $v_{i} = v_{p} cos (t/RC)$. The steady state output $v_{o}$

detailed_solution.concept: Network Theory - Sinusoidal Steady State Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: Redrawing the circuits-domain $$\begin{aligned} V_{i}(s) &=\left(R+\frac{1}{s C}\right) I(s)+\frac{R \cdot \frac{1}{s C}}{R+\frac{1}{s C}} I(s) \\ V_{i}(s) &=\frac{1+s C R}{s C} I(s)+\frac{R}{1+s C R} I(s) \\ \because \quad v_{i} &=V_{p} \cos (t / R C) \qquad \ldots(i)\\ \text{so here,} \qquad \omega&=\frac{1}{R C} \\ Now,V_{i}(s)&=\frac{(1+j \omega C R)}{j \omega C} I(s)+\frac{R}{(1+j \omega C R)} I(s) \\ \text{Put,}\quad \omega&=\frac{1}{R C} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} \text { So, } \quad V_{i}(s)&=\left[\frac{(1+j) R}{j}+\frac{R}{1+j}\right] I(s)\\ \frac{V_{i}(s)}{I(s)} &=\frac{3 R}{(1+j)} \qquad\ldots(ii)\\ I(s) &=\frac{V_{i}(s)}{3 R} \times(1+j) \\ \text { Now, } V_{0}(s) &=\left(R \| \frac{1}{s C}\right) I(s) \\ \Rightarrow \quad V_{0}(s) &=\frac{R \cdot \frac{1}{s C}}{R+\frac{1}{s C}} I(s) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \quad V_{0}(s)&=\frac{R}{1+S C R} \cdot \frac{V_{i}(s)}{3 R}(1+j) \\ \Rightarrow \quad V_{0}(s)&=\frac{R}{1+j} \cdot \frac{V_{i}(s)}{3 R}(1+j) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \quad V_{0}(s)&=\frac{V_{i}(s)}{3} \\ \text{In time domain,}\\ v_{0}(t)&=\frac{1}{3} v_{i}(t) \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{0}(t)&=\frac{V_{p}}{3} \cos \left(\frac{t}{R C}\right) \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q14.question: The solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx}=ky,y(0)=c$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \frac{d y}{d x}&=k y\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{y}&=k d x \\ \end{aligned}$$

Integrating both sides

$$\begin{aligned} \ln y &=k x+A \\ \text{Put}\quad x &=0 \\ \ln y(0)&=A \\ A&=\ln c &[\because y(0)=c] \\ \text{Hence. }\quad \ln y&=k x+\ln c \\ \Rightarrow \ln y-\ln c&=k x \\ \Rightarrow \quad \ln \left(\frac{y}{c}\right)&=k x \\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{y}{c}&=e^{k x} \\ \text{or}\quad y&=c e^{k x} \end{aligned}$$

Taking Laplace transform of both sides

$100 s^{2} Y(s)-20 s Y(s)+Y(s)=\frac{X(s)}{s}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{Y(s)}{X(s)}=\frac{1 / s}{\left(100 s^{2}-20 s+1\right)}=\frac{1}{s(10 s-1)^{2}}$

As poles are on the right-hand side of s-plane so given system is unstable system.

pp:ec:2011:q26.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 26
pp:ec:2011:q26.question: A current sheet $\bar{J}$ = 10$\hat{u}_{y}$ A/m lies on the dielectric interface $x=0$ between two dielectric media with $\varepsilon _{r1}$=5, $\mu _{r1}$=1 in Region-1 $(x \lt 0)$ and $\varepsilon _{r2}$=5, $\mu _{r2}$=2 in Region-2 $(x \gt 0)$. If the magnetic field in Region-1 at $x = 0^{-}$ is $\vec{H}_{1} = 3\hat{u}_{x}$ + 30$\hat{u}_{y}$ A/m. The magnetic field in Region-2 at $x = 0^{+}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
For magnetic field boundary relations are

$$\begin{aligned} \vec{B}_{n_{1}} &=\vec{B}_{n_{2}} \\ \text { and } \vec{H}_{t_{1}}-\vec{H}_{t_{2}} &=-\vec{J}_{s} \times \vec{a}_{n} \\ \Rightarrow \quad B_{x_{1}}&=B_{x_{2}}\qquad\text{(x is normal component)}\\ \mu_{1} H_{x_{1}} &=\mu_{2} H_{x 2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1 \times 3 &=2 \times H_{x 2} \\ H_{x_{2}} &=1.5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \vec{H}_{11}-\vec{H}_{t_{2}} &=-10 \hat{u}_{y} \times \hat{u}_{x}=+10 \hat{u}_{z} \\ \vec{H}_{t_{2}} &=H_{t_{1}}-10 \hat{u}_{z} \\ \vec{H}_{t_{2}} &=30 \hat{u}_{y}-10 \hat{u}_{z} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \vec{H}_{2} &=1.5 \hat{u}_{x}+30 \hat{u}_{y}-10 \hat{u}_{z} \mathrm{A} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q27.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 27
pp:ec:2011:q27.question:
A transmission line of characteristic impedance 50$\Omega$ is terminated in a load
impedance $Z_{L}$. The VSWR of the line is measured as 5 and the first of the
voltage maxima in the line is observed at a distance of $\frac{\lambda }{4}$ from the load. The value of $Z_{L}$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\text { VSWR }=5=\frac{1+|\Gamma|}{1-|\Gamma|}$

$\therefore |\Gamma|=\frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow \Gamma=\pm \frac{2}{3}$

If maximum is at $\lambda / 4$ from load then minimum will be at load itself.

For the phase of $\Gamma$

$2 \beta x_{\max }=2 n \pi+\theta$

where $x_{\max }$ is distance of $V_{\max }$ from load.

$$\begin{aligned} 2 \cdot \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \cdot \frac{\lambda}{4}&=\theta \\ \Gamma&=-\frac{2}{3}\\ \text{Now},-\frac{2}{3}&=\frac{Z_{L}-Z_{0}}{Z_{L}+Z_{0}}=\frac{Z_{L}-50}{Z_{L}+50}\\ \Rightarrow Z_{L}&=10 \Omega \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q28.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ec:2011:q28.question: X(t) is a stationary random process with auto-correlation function $R_{x}(\tau )=exp(-\pi \tau^{2})$. This process is passed through the system shown below. The power spectral density of the output process Y(t) is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} y(t) &=\frac{d}{d t} x(t)-x(t) \\ \mathrm{FT} \rightarrow \quad Y(f) &=j 2 \pi f x(t)-x(f) \\ Y(t) &=[j 2 \pi f-1] \mathrm{x}(f) \\ \mathrm{PSD} \rightarrow \quad S_{Y}(f) &=|j 2 \pi f-1|^{2} S_{X}(f) \\ S_{r}(f) &=\left(4 \pi^{2} f^{2}+1\right) S_{X}(f) \\ S_{X}(f) &=F T\left[R_{X}(\tau)\right] \\ S_{X}(f) &=e^{-\pi f^{2}} \end{aligned}$$ $\because$[Gaussian function $\stackrel{FT}{\longrightarrow}$ Gaussian function] $S_{Y}(t)=\left[4 \pi^{2} f^{2}+1\right] e^{-\pi f^{2}}$

pp:ec:2011:q31.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 31
pp:ec:2011:q31.question: In the circuit shown below, for the MOS transistors, $\mu _{n}C_{OX}=100\mu A/V^{2}$ and the threshold voltage $V_{T}$ = 1V. The voltage $V_{x}$ at the source of the upper transistor is

detailed_solution.concept: Analog Circuits - FET and MOSFET Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown:
For upper MOS,

$$\begin{aligned} V_{D S} &=6-V_{x} \\ V_{G S}-V_{T} &=5-V_{x}-1 \\ &=4-V_{x} \end{aligned}$$

Upper MOS will be in saturation because

$V_{D S}>V_{G S}-V_{T}$

For lower MOS,

$$\begin{array}{c} V_{D S}=V_{x} \\ V_{G S}-V_{T}=V_{x}-1\\ \text{SO}\quad V_{D S}>V_{G S}-V_{T} \end{array}$$

Hence both MOS will be in saturation

$$\begin{aligned} I_{D 1}&=\mu_{n} C_{o x}\left(\frac{W}{L}\right)\left(V_{G S}-V_{T}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad I_{D 1}&=\mu_{n} C_{O x}(4)\left(4-V_{x}\right)^{2}\\ \text{Similarly,} \quad I_{D 2}&=\mu_{n} C_{o x}(1)\left(V_{x}-1\right)^{2} \\ \text{but, }\quad I_{D 1}&=I_{D 2} \\ \therefore \mu_{n} C_{o x}(4)\left(4-V_{x}\right)^{2}&=\mu_{n} C_{o x}(1)\left(V_{x}-1\right)^{2} \\ \text{On solving, }V_{x}&=3 \text{volt} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q34.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ec:2011:q34.question: If $F(s)=L[f(t)]=\frac{2(s+1)}{s^{2}+4s+7}$ then the initial and final values of $f(t)$ are respectively

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} F(s)&=L[f(t)]=\frac{2(s+1)}{s^{2}+4 s+7}\\ \text{Initial value,}\\ \lim _{t \rightarrow 0} f(t) &=\lim _{s \rightarrow \infty} s F(s)=\lim _{s \rightarrow \infty} s \cdot \frac{2(s+1)}{s^{2}+4 s+7} \\ &=\lim _{s \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2 s^{2}\left(1+\frac{1}{s}\right)}{s^{2}\left(1+\frac{4}{s}+\frac{7}{s^{2}}\right)} \\ &=\frac{2(1+0)}{(1+0+0)}=2\\ \text{Final value,}\\ \lim _{t \rightarrow \infty} f(t) &=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s F(s)=\lim _{s \rightarrow 0} s \cdot \frac{2(s+1)}{s^{2}+4 s+7} \\ &=0 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q36.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ec:2011:q36.question:
A numerical solution of the equation $f(x)=x + \sqrt{x}-3= 0$ can be obtained using
Newton- Raphson method. If the starting value is $x = 2$ for the iteration, the
value of $x$ that is to be used in the next step is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} x_{n+1} &=x_{n}-\frac{f\left(x_{n}\right)}{f^{\prime}\left(x_{n}\right)} \\ x=2,\quad f\left(x_{0}\right)&=2+\sqrt{2}-3=\sqrt{2}-1 \\ f(x)&=1+\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}} \\ \text { Then, } \quad x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left(x_{0}\right)}{f^{\prime}\left(x_{0}\right)} \\ &=2-\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{1+\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}&=1.694 \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q37.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ec:2011:q37.question:
The electric and magnetic fields for a TEM wave of frequency 14 GHz in a homogeneous medium of relative permittivity er and relative permeability $\mu _{r}$=1 are given by
$\vec{E}=E_{p}e^{j(\omega t-280\pi t)}\hat{u}_{z} V/m$
$\vec{H}=3e^{j(\omega t-280\pi y)}\hat{u}_{x} V/m$

Assuming the speed of light in free space to be $3 \times 10^{8}$ m/s, the intrinsic impedance of free space to be 120$\pi$, the relative permittivity $\varepsilon_{r}$ of the medium and the electric field amplitude $E_{p}$ are

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Given:}\quad\vec{E}&=E_{p} e^{i(\omega t-280 \pi y)} \hat{u}_{z} V / m\\ \vec{H}&=3 e^{i(\omega t-280 \pi y)} \hat{u}_{x} A / m \\ v&=3 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}$$

From given expression we conclude that,

$$\begin{aligned} \beta &=280 \pi=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \\ \therefore \quad & \lambda=\frac{1}{140} \text { meter } \\ v &=f \lambda=14 \times 10^{9} \times \frac{1}{140} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{se} \\ v &=1 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \text { but, } \quad v &=\frac{c}{\sqrt{\epsilon_{r} \mu_{r}}} \\ \therefore \quad 1 \times 10^{8} &=\frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{\sqrt{1 \times \epsilon_{r}}} \\ \therefore \quad \epsilon_{r}&=9\\ \frac{E_{P}}{H_{P}}&=\eta=\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{\epsilon}}=\sqrt{\frac{\mu_{0} \times 1}{\epsilon_{0} \times 9}}=\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{\frac{\mu_{0}}{\epsilon_{0}}} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{E_{P}}{3}&=\frac{1}{3} \times 120 \pi \\ \therefore \quad E_{P}&=120 \pi \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q38.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ec:2011:q38.question:
A message signal $m(t) = \cos 2000 \pi t + 4 \cos 4000 \pi t$ modulates the carrier
$c(t) = \cos 2 \pi f_{c} t$ where $f_{c}$=1MHz to produce an AM signal. For demodulating the generated AM signal using an envelope detector, the time constant RC of the detector circuit should satisfy

From Question,

$$\begin{aligned} y &=\left[y_{1} y_{2}\right]^{\top}=[12]^{\top}=\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\2\end{array}\right] \\ \dot{x}_{1}(t) &=-2 x_{1}(t)+u(t) \\ \dot{x}_{2}(t) &=-2 x_{2}(t)+u(t) \\ \left[\begin{array}{c}\dot{x}_{1} \\\dot{x}_{2}\end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{cc}-2 & 0 \\-2 & 0\end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{l}x_{1} \\x_{2} \end{array}\right]+\left[\begin{array}{l}1 \\1\end{array}\right] u(t) \\ \dot{x} &=[-2] x+[1] u \end{aligned}$$

only option (B) is satisfied.

pp:ec:2011:q40.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ec:2011:q40.question: Two systems $H_{1}(z)$ and $H_{2}(z)$ are connected in cascade as shown below. The overall output $y(n)$ is the same as the input $x(n)$ with a one unit delay. The transfer function of the second system $H_{2}(z)$ is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$y[n]=x[n-1]$

Taking z-transform of both sides

$$\begin{aligned} r(z) &=z^{-1} X(z) \\ \frac{\gamma(z)}{X(z)} &=z^{-1} \end{aligned}$$

For cascaded system

$$\begin{aligned} H(z)&=H_{1}(z) \cdot H_{2}(z)\\ z^{-1} &=\frac{\left(1-0.4 z^{-1}\right)}{\left(1-0.6 z^{-1}\right)^{-1}(z)} \\ \therefore \quad H_{2}(z) &=\frac{z^{-1}\left(1-0.6 z^{-1}\right)}{\left(1-0.4 z^{-1}\right)} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q42.question: The first six points of the 8-point DFT of a real valued sequence are 5, 1-j3, 0, 3-j4, 0 and 3+j4. The last two points of the DFT are respectively

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} V(0) &=V\left(0^{+}\right)=\frac{Q}{C} \\ &=\frac{2.5 \times 10^{-3}}{50 \times 10^{-6}}=-50 \mathrm{V} \\ & \quad\because \text{(direction given is opposite)}\\ V(\infty)&=100 \mathrm{V} \end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned} V(t) &=V(\infty)+\left[V\left(0^{+}\right)-V(\infty)\right] e^{-\theta \tau} \\ &=100+(-50-100) e^{-j \tau} \\ V(t) &=100-150 e^{-t t} \\ i(t) &=C \frac{d V}{d t}=C \frac{150}{\tau} e^{-t / \tau} \\ \text { and } \tau &=10 \times 50 \times 10^{-6} \\ &=5 \times 10^{-4}\\ i(t) &=50 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{150}{10 \times 50 \times 10^{-6}} e^{-2 \times 10^{3} t} \\ &=15 e^{-2 \times 10^{3} t} \mathrm{Amp} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ec:2011:q46.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:ec:2011:q46.question:
The system of equations
x + y + z = 6
x + 4y + 6y = 20
x + 4y + $\lambda$z =$\mu$
has NO solution for values of $\lambda$ and $\mu$ given by

detailed_solution.markdown:
The augumented matrix for the system of

equations is

$$\begin{aligned} [A: B]&=\left[\begin{array}{lll|l} 1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 6 & 20 \\ 1 & 4 & \lambda & \mu \end{array}\right] \\ [A: B]&=\left[\begin{array}{lll|l} 1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 1 & 4 & 6 & 20 \\ 0 & 0 & \lambda-6 & \mu-20 \end{array}\right] \quad\left[R_{3} \rightarrow R_{3}-R_{2}\right] \end{aligned}$$

If $\lambda=6$ and $\mu \neq 20$ then

$$\begin{aligned} & \rho(A: B)=3 \text { and } \rho(A)=2 \\ \because \quad & \rho(A: B) \neq \rho(A) \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Given system of equations has no solution

for $\lambda=6$ and $\mu \neq 20$

pp:ec:2011:q47.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ec:2011:q47.question:
A fair dice is tossed two times. The probability that the second toss results in a
value that is higher than the first toss is

detailed_solution.markdown:
In the first toss, results can be 1,2,3,4,5

For 1, the second toss results can be 2,3,4,5,6

For 2 , the second toss results can be 3,4,5,6

For 3, the second toss results can be 4,5,6

For 4, the second toss results can be 5,6

For 5, the second toss results can be 6

The required probability

$=\frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{5}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{4}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{3}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{2}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{12}$

pp:ec:2011:q49.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 49
pp:ec:2011:q49.question:
The channel resistance of an N-channel JFET shown in the figure below is 600 $\Omega$ when the full channel thickness ($t_{ch}$) of 10 $\mu m$ is available for conduction. The built-in voltage of the gate $P^+ N$ junction ($V_{bi}$) is -1 V. When the gate to source voltage ($V_{GS}$) is 0 V, the channel is depleted by 1 $\mu m$ on each side due to the builtin voltage and hence the thickness available for conduction is only 8 $\mu m$.

The channel resistance when $V_{GS}$ =0 V is

detailed_solution.concept: Electronic Devices - BJT and FET Basics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Depletion layer width

$$\begin{aligned} w &\propto \sqrt{V_{G S}+V_{b i}}\\ \text { Given, } & V_{b i}=-1 \\ \text { and for, } & V_{G S}=0 \mathrm{V}, w_{1}=1 \mu \mathrm{m}\\ \text{Now for, }\quad V_{G S}&=-3 \mathrm{V}, w_{2} \text{ can be calculated}\\ \text{as }\quad \frac{w_{1}}{w_{2}}&=\sqrt{\frac{0-1}{-3-1}}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad w_{2}&=2 \mu m \\ \end{aligned}$$

Channel width $\uparrow \Rightarrow$ channel resistance $\uparrow$

For $10 \mu \mathrm{m}$ channel resistance $=600 \Omega$

For $8 \mu \mathrm{m}$ channel resistance

$=\frac{600 \times 100}{8}=750 \Omega$

pp:ec:2011:q50.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 50
pp:ec:2011:q50.question:
The input-output transfer function of a plant $H(s)=\frac{100}{s(s+10)^2}$. The plant is placed in a unity negative feedback configuration as shown in the figure below.

The gain margin of the system under closed loop unity negative feedback is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} G(s) H(s) &=\frac{100}{s(s+10)^{2}} \\ \phi &=-90^{\circ}-2 \tan ^{-1}(\omega / 10) \end{aligned}$$

For phase cross-over frequency, $\phi=-180^{\circ}$

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad-180 &=-90^{\circ}-2 \tan ^{-1}(\omega / 10) \\ \Rightarrow & \omega=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec} \\ s &=j \omega \\ \text { Put, } \quad G(j \omega) H(j \omega) &=\frac{100}{j \omega(j \omega+100)^{2}} \\ |G(j \omega) H(j \omega)|_{\omega=10} &=\frac{100}{\omega\left(\omega^{2}+100\right)} \\ &=\frac{100}{10(200)}=\frac{1}{20} \\ \text { G.M. } &=\frac{1}{\mid G(j \omega) H(j \omega)}=20 \end{aligned}$$

G.M. in $\mathrm{dB}=20 \log 20=26 \mathrm{dB}$

pp:ec:2011:q54.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 54
pp:ec:2011:q54.question:
A four-phase and an eight-phase signal constellation are shown in the figure below.

For the constraint that the minimum distance between pairs of signal points be d for both constellations, the radii $r_{1}$, and $r_{2}$ of the circles are

detailed_solution.markdown:
For M-ary

$d=2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{M}\right) \sqrt{E_{s}}$

Distance of any point from origin is $\sqrt{E}_{s}$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{For, 4-ary}, r_{1}&=\sqrt{E_{s_{1}}} \\ 8-\text { ary, } \quad r_{2}&=\sqrt{E_{s_{2}}}\\ \text { For, } 4-\text { ary } M=4, d_{1}&=2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) r_{1} \\ 8-\text { ary } M=8 ; d_{2}&=2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right) r_{2} \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{array}{l} \text { if } d_{1}=d_{2}=d \text { then } \\ 2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) r_{1}=d \Rightarrow r_{1}=\frac{d}{\sqrt{2}}=0,707 d \\ 2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right) r_{2}=d \\ \Rightarrow r_{2}=\frac{d}{2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)}=1.307 d \end{array}$$

pp:ec:2011:q55.title: GATE EC 2011 | Set 1 | Question: 55
pp:ec:2011:q55.question:
A four-phase and an eight-phase signal constellation are shown in the figure below.

Assuming high SNR and that all signals are equally probable, the additional average transmitted signal energy required by the 8-PSK signal to achieve the same error probability as the 4-PSK signal is

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P_{e} \propto \sqrt{E_{s}}$ for both cases

$SO, \frac{\sqrt{E_{s}}}{\sqrt{E_{s_{2}}}}=\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}=\frac{0.707 d}{1.307 d}$

$\Rightarrow \quad \frac{E_{s_{2}}}{E_{s_{1}}}=\left(\frac{1.307}{0.707}\right)^{2}=3.42$

To achieve same error, $2^{\text {nd }}$ must have 3.42 time than $1^{\text {st. }}$

The value in $\mathrm{dB}=10 \log (3.42)=5.33 \mathrm{dB}$
